    {"name": "SPlisHSPlasH", "url": "https://github.com/InteractiveComputerGraphics/SPlisHSPlasH/tree/2.18.1"},
    {"name": "splashsurf", "url": "https://github.com/InteractiveComputerGraphics/splashsurf/tree/56d3e6a"},

  ],
  "on_screen_text": "SPlisHSPlasH | Today's open-source project is SPlisHSPlasH, 오늘의 오픈소스는 SPlisHSPlasH입니다. | 71,346 particles · colour = speed   t = 0.00 s | It uses smoothed particle hydrodynamics, or SPH. 평활 입자 유체역학, 줄여서 SPH를 씁니다. | slice through the middle of the tank   t = 0.54 s | To find the density at a particle, 한 입자의 밀도를 구하려면 | closer neighbours count more (kernel weight)   t = 0.54 s | 41 neighbours (in 3D) + itself | Here that's 41 neighbors, 여기서는 이웃이 41개이고 | density in the same slice   t = 0.21 s | below 1,000 kg/m³   1,000  +0.5% | Real water barely compresses. 실제 물은 거의 압축되지 않습니다. | README | License | build-linux build-windows-wheels build-macos build-mac-wheels docs | SPlisHSPlasH is an Open-source library for the physically-based simulation of fluids. The simulation in this library is based on the Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics | README | License | SPlisHSPlasH is an open-source library for the physically-based simulation of fluids. The simulation in this library is based on the Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) method which is a popular meshless Lagrangian approach to simulate complex fluid effects. The SPH formalism allows an efficient computation of a certain quantity of a fluid particle by considering only a finite set of neighboring particles. One of the most important research topics in the field of SPH methods is the simulation of... | how far each neighbour is (up to 4 r)   0 ... distance to the neighbour ... 4 r = 6.4 cm | density in the same slice   t = 1.58 s | below 1,000 kg/m³   1,000  +0.5% | average compression, all 71,346 particles: 0.010 % | @index.opensource | @hyun2xyz | Its DFSPH solver repeats that correction, DFSPH 솔버는 이 보정을 반복합니다. | Thank you. 고맙습니다. | README | License | Features | SPlisHSPlasH implements: an open-source SPH fluid simulation (2D & 3D); neighborhood search on CPU or GPU; supports vectorization using AVX; Python binding (thanks to Stefan Jeske); supports embedded Python scripts; several implicit pressure solvers (WCSPH, PCISPH, PBF, IISPH, DFSPH, PF); explicit and implicit viscosity methods; current surface tension approaches; different vorticity methods; computation of drag forces; support for multi-phase simulations",
  "key_claims": [
    "The scene is a dam-break water simulation with 71,346 particles",
    "SPlisHSPlasH uses smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) to simulate the fluid",
    "Density at a particle is estimated by summing neighbor mass within a radius, weighted by a smooth kernel; here each particle has 41 neighbors",
    "The resulting density is about 1,000 kg/m³, matching real water",
    "Real water barely compresses, so the DFSPH solver repeatedly corrects pressure to keep compression low (average compression 0.010% across all 71,346 particles)",
    "Each simulation step finds neighbors, solves for pressure, adds gravity and viscosity, and moves every particle",
    "4 seconds of simulated motion took 3,052 steps and about 14 minutes on one CPU core, not counting rendering",
    "The workflow is SPlisHSPlasH simulation → splashsurf surface reconstruction → Mitsuba rendering",
    "splashsurf wraps the raw particles into a smooth surface, and Mitsuba renders it to look like water",
    "The water sequences in the reel are shown in 2x slow motion",
    "SPlisHSPlasH is open source under the MIT license; splashsurf is also MIT; Mitsuba is BSD-3-Clause"
  ],
  "info_channel": "caption"
}
